Rashi on Eruvin 93b:10:1.hebrew: דיורין הבאין בשבת - כגון כותל שבין שתי חצירות שנפל בשבת, דהיינו דיורייהו השתא כי הדדי:
Rashi on Eruvin 93b:10:1.english: Residents who arrive on Shabbat - For example, a wall between two courtyards that collapsed on Shabbat, so that their dwelling is now together.

Rashi on Eruvin 93b:10:2.english: What is [the ruling as to whether] they render [it] prohibited - Upon one another.

Rashi on Eruvin 93b:11:1.hebrew: וקטנה אסורה - [וס"ד] שנפרצה בשבת:
Rashi on Eruvin 93b:11:1.english: And the small [courtyard] is prohibited - [And it would enter your mind] that it was breached on Shabbat.

Rashi on Eruvin 93b:12:1.hebrew: אלא ודאי - על כורחיך הכי תוקמא, דהא את אמרת: דיורין הבאין בשבת אין אוסרין:
Rashi on Eruvin 93b:12:1.english: Rather, certainly - Perforce you must establish it so, for you said: Residents who arrive on Shabbat do not prohibit.

Rashi on Eruvin 93b:12:2.english: For you said: I inquired of Rav Huna: [If] one established an eiruv via the opening - Two courtyards that established an eiruv together by means of the opening between them:

Rashi on Eruvin 93b:12:3.english: And it was sealed - On Shabbat, in that a collapse [of rubble] fell opposite it.

Rashi on Eruvin 93b:12:4.hebrew: מהו - לטלטל מזו לזו דרך גובה הכותל וחורין וסדקין: מי אמרינן, "הואיל והותר למקצת שבת הותר לכולה", או לא:
Rashi on Eruvin 93b:12:4.english: What is [the halakha] - [Regarding] carrying from this [courtyard] to that [courtyard] over the top of the wall and [through] holes and crevices: Do we say, "Since it was permitted for part of Shabbat, it is permitted for all of it," or not?

Rashi on Eruvin 93b:13:1.hebrew: כותל שבין שתי חצירות - שלא היה פתח ביניהם, ולא עירבו בו יחד, ונפל:
Rashi on Eruvin 93b:13:1.english: A wall between two courtyards - Where there was no doorway between them, and they had not made an eiruv together through it, and [the wall] collapsed.

Rashi on Eruvin 93b:13:2.hebrew: רב אמר אין מטלטלין בו אלא בארבע - רב לית ליה: הואיל והותרה — הותרה. וכחד חצר לא משוינן ליה — דקי"ל: חצר שלא עירבה, דברי הכל מטלטלין כלים ששבתו באוירא, דההיא כולה חדא רשותא היא; אבל הכא, ב' רשויות האסורות זו עם זו היו, ונמצאת כל אחת פרוצה במלואה למקום האסור לה. אע"ג דקי"ל דחצירות רשות אחת הן — הכא בשעירבה כל אחת לעצמה עסקינן, ורב לטעמיה, דאמר: הלכה כר"ש, והוא שלא עירבו; אבל עירבו — שתי רשויות הן:
Rashi on Eruvin 93b:13:2.english: Rav said: One may carry in it only within four [cubits] - Rav does not accept [the principle that] since it was permitted, it remains permitted. And we do not treat it as a single courtyard — for [although] we maintain that [in] a courtyard whose [residents] did not establish an eiruv, all agree that one may carry vessels that rested in the open [courtyard at the onset of Shabbat], since that is entirely a single domain; but here, they were two domains that were forbidden to one another, and each [courtyard] is [now] found to be breached in its entirety into an area that is forbidden to it. Even though we maintain that courtyards are a single domain, here we are dealing with [a case] where each [courtyard] established an eiruv for itself; and Rav [follows] his [own] reasoning, as he said: The halakhah follows Rabbi Shimon [only] provided that they did not establish an eiruv, but if they established an eiruv, they are two [separate] domains.

Rashi on Eruvin 93b:2:1.hebrew: גידוד חמשה - חצר שקרקעיתה גבוה חמשה טפחים, והוסיפו על אותו גובה מחיצה ה':
Rashi on Eruvin 93b:2:1.english: An embankment of five - A courtyard whose ground is five handbreadths high, and they added a partition of five [handbreadths] onto that height.

Rashi on Eruvin 93b:3:1.hebrew: מודה רב חסדא בתחתונה - דלגבה הויא מחיצה, אבל לגבי עליונה לאו מחיצה היא, שאינה רואה את פני עשרה למחיצתה. ואי הויא כוליה בגידוד — שפיר טפי, משום דמשתמשא להדיא עד סוף הגידוד, ורואה גובהה יותר על חברתה עשרה, ומינכרא מחיצתה:
Rashi on Eruvin 93b:3:1.english: Rav Ḥisda concedes with regard to the lower [courtyard] - For with respect to it, it is a partition; but with respect to the upper [courtyard], it is not a partition, as it does not face ten [handbreadths] for its partition. And had it been entirely an embankment, [it would be] much better, because it uses [the ground] directly up to the edge of the embankment, and sees its height ten [handbreadths] higher than that of its fellow, and its partition is evident.

Rashi on Eruvin 93b:3:2.hebrew: תחתונה תרי תערב - כלומר, לעצמה תיערב דיוריה, ולא עם עליונה, שהרי מחיצה ביניהם. אבל עליונה — אפילו לעצמה אסורה, שהתחתונה אוסרתה, שאין כאן מחיצה; ולא חד נמי תערב עם תחתונה, שהרי אין כאן פתח, דלגבי תחתונה הכל סתום:
Rashi on Eruvin 93b:3:2.english: The lower [courtyard] should establish two - That is to say, for itself it may establish an eiruv for its residents, and not with the upper [courtyard], for behold, there is a partition between them. But the upper [courtyard], even for itself is forbidden [to carry in], for the lower [courtyard] restricts it, since there is no partition here; nor can it establish one [eiruv] either with the lower [courtyard], for behold, there is no entrance here, as with respect to the lower [courtyard], everything is sealed.

Rashi on Eruvin 93b:4:1.hebrew: במגופפת - מחיצה עשרה על הגידוד, עד עשר אמות אמצעיות שהניחוה כעין פתח, ולא הניחו שם המחיצה עשרה, אלא מחיצה חמשה והגידוד חמשה. הלכך, שתיהן מערבות לעצמן, ואין זו אוסרת על זו — דלגבי תחתונה כולה סתומה היא, ולגבי עליונה [מחיצה] ופתחא היא. ומיהו, כי הדדי לא מצו מערבי, משום דלגבי תחתונה הכל סתום:
Rashi on Eruvin 93b:4:1.english: [Where it was] flanked - [There was] a partition of ten [handbreadths] on [top of] the embankment, up to the middle ten cubits, which they left as a sort of entrance, and they did not place the partition of ten there, but rather a partition of five and the embankment of five. Therefore, both of them may establish an eiruv for themselves, and neither restricts the other, for with respect to the lower [courtyard], it is completely closed off, and with respect to the upper [courtyard], it is [a partition] and an entrance. However, they cannot establish an eiruv together, because with respect to the lower [courtyard], everything is closed off.

Rashi on Eruvin 93b:5:1.hebrew: אימא סיפא כו' - ועל כרחך, האי ״פחות מכאן״ אמחיצת חמשה שבעשר האמות קאי, דהא בכל ההיקף מחיצה עשרה איכא:
Rashi on Eruvin 93b:5:1.english: Say the latter clause, etc. - And perforce, this [phrase,] “less than this,” refers to the partition of five [handbreadths] that is within the ten cubits, since along the entire perimeter there is a partition of ten [handbreadths].

Rashi on Eruvin 93b:5:2.english: If they wish, they establish one [eiruv] - For it is a full-fledged entrance with respect to both of them.

Rashi on Eruvin 93b:6:1.hebrew: במלואה - שאין ברחבה אלא עשר אמות. הלכך, אסרה עליונה עליה, ולא מערבה בהדה, כדתנן: גדולה מותרת וקטנה אסורה:
Rashi on Eruvin 93b:6:1.english: In its entirety - For its width is only ten cubits. Therefore, the upper [courtyard] renders [carrying] prohibited for it, and it does not establish an eiruv with it, as we learned in the Mishnah: The large [courtyard] is permitted and the small [courtyard] is prohibited.

Rashi on Eruvin 93b:7:1.english: If so, the lower [courtyard] should establish one [eiruv] - With the upper [courtyard].

Rashi on Eruvin 93b:7:2.hebrew: תרי לא תערב - בפני עצמה, דעליונה אוסרת אא"כ עירבה עמה:
Rashi on Eruvin 93b:7:2.english: It may not establish two - By itself, for the upper [courtyard] renders [it] forbidden unless it established an eiruv with it.

Tosafot on Eruvin 93b:12:1.hebrew: שבת כיון שהותרה הותרה - פירשתי בפרק קמא (דף יז. ד"ה עירוב):
Tosafot on Eruvin 93b:12:1.english: "Shabbat, once it was permitted, it was permitted" - I explained [this] in the first chapter (17a, s.v. Eiruv).

Tosafot on Eruvin 93b:13:1.hebrew: אין מטלטלין בה אלא בארבע - בכלים ששבתו בבית, לר"ש:
Tosafot on Eruvin 93b:13:1.english: "One may carry in it only within four [cubits]" - [This refers to] utensils that rested in the house, according to Rabbi Shimon.

Tosafot on Eruvin 93b:1:1.hebrew: גידוד חמשה ומחיצה חמשה אין מצטרפין - בפרק שני דגיטין (דף טו:) פי' בקונטרס: כגון בית עמוק חמשה, ויש לו מחיצות חמשה — אין מצטרפין להיות תוכו רה"י. וקשיא לר"ת: דהא אמר בפרק בתרא (דף צט:) דבור וחוליתה מצטרפין! ובשמעתא נמי אמר דמודה רב חסדא בתחתונה, הואיל ורואה פני י'. אלא יש לפרש: "גידוד חמשה" — גבוה חמשה, ונפקא מינה בשתי חצירות זו למעלה מזו, ולעליונה כדאמר הכא. וצ"ע לענין שבת: אם יש (לפרש כשיש) תל ברה"ר גבוה חמשה ורחב ארבעה, ועל גביו עשו מחיצה חמשה — שהזורק מרה"ר לתוכו חייב, ומתוכו לרה"ר פטור:
Tosafot on Eruvin 93b:1:1.english: An embankment of five and a partition of five do not combine - In the second chapter of Gittin (15b), Rashi explained: For example, a house that is five handbreadths deep and has partitions of five handbreadths, they do not combine to make its interior a private domain. And this is difficult for Rabbeinu Tam: for the Gemara says in the final chapter of Eruvin (99b) that a pit and its embankment combine! And in our sugya as well, it says that Rav Chisda concedes regarding the lower courtyard, since it sees the face of ten handbreadths. Rather, it should be explained: "An embankment of five" means five handbreadths high, and the practical difference is in two courtyards, one above the other, and regarding the upper one, as it says here. And it requires further study regarding the matter of Shabbat: If there is (to explain: when there is) a mound in the public domain five handbreadths high and four handbreadths wide, and on top of it they made a partition of five handbreadths — whether one who throws from the public domain into it is liable, and one who throws from within it into the public domain is exempt.

Tosafot on Eruvin 93b:8:1.hebrew: וכי קתני פחות מכאן מערבין אחד ואין מערבין שנים אתחתונה - וא"ת: לעיל, כדפריך "עליונה לא תערב לא חד ולא תרי", אמאי לא משני: הא דקתני "מערבין שנים ואין מערבין אחד" — אתחתונה? ויש לומר: משום דמשמע ליה "מערבין שנים" — אתרוייהו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 93b:8:1.english: And when it teaches: "Less than this, they establish one and do not establish two," [it is referring] to the lower [courtyard] - And if you say: Above, when [the Gemara] objected, "The upper [courtyard] should establish neither one [eiruv] nor two," why did it not answer that that which it teaches, "they establish two and do not establish one," [is referring] to the lower [courtyard]? And one can say: Because "they establish two" implied to it [that it applies] to both of them.

Tosafot on Eruvin 93b:9:1.hebrew: לא תימא אימר אלא ודאי מבעוד יום נפרצה - קשה: דהכא אמר אביי דרבה סבר כשמואל, דאמר: שבת, הואיל והותרה — הותרה; וא"כ תיקשי, דאביי גופיה אמר (שבת דף כב.): כל מילי דמר עביד כחומרי דרב, בר מהני תלת דעביד כשמואל: מתירין מבגד לבגד כו'! ואין לומר דמש"ה לא חשיב הא דהכא משום דרב הונא ורב יהודה נמי סברי כשמואל — דהא בגרירא איכא דסברי כשמואל, דהא בפרק המוציא (שבת פא.) משמע דסבר רבי יוחנן כסתם משנה דנזיר: חופף ומפספס. ומיהו י"ל, דהכי פריך בהמוציא: ומי מצי ר' יוחנן למימר דבר שאין מתכוין אסור, דלא כסתם משנה דנזיר, אפילו איכא סתמא אחרינא? כדאשכחן בביצה (דף כג:): מאי אולמיה האי סתמא מהאי? ואין לרבי יוחנן נמי לפסוק כשום אחת בלא ראייה. אי נמי, יש לומר: הא דעביד כחומרי דרב — היינו בעלמא, לבד מעירוב ואבל, דהלכה כדברי המיקל בהם. או שמא, כיון דזימנין הך קולא הויא חומרא — כגון דנאסר במקצת שבת, דמהאי טעמא נאסר לכל השבת — לא חשיב ליה מחומרי דרב, דלרב לית ליה הואיל והותרה הותרה, ולית ליה נמי הואיל ונאסר נאסר:
Tosafot on Eruvin 93b:9:1.english: Do not say: "Say [it was breached on Shabbat]"; rather, it was certainly breached while it was still day - This is difficult: For here Abaye says that Rabba holds in accordance with [the view of] Shmuel, who said: [Regarding] Shabbat, since it was permitted [at its onset], it remains permitted. And if so, it presents a difficulty, for Abaye himself said (Shabbat 22a): "In all matters, the Master [Rabba] acted in accordance with the stringencies of Rav, except for these three where he acted in accordance with [the lenient view of] Shmuel: [namely,] one may untie [tzitzit] from garment to garment, etc."! And one cannot say that for this reason he did not count this [case] here, because Rav Huna and Rav Yehuda also hold like Shmuel — for regarding dragging [a bench on dirt], there are [others] who hold like Shmuel, as in the chapter [entitled] HaMotzi (Shabbat 81b) it implies that Rabbi Yochanan holds like the anonymous Mishnah in Nazir [that a nazirite] scrubs and parts [his hair]. And yet, one can say that this is what [the Gemara] challenges in HaMotzi: Could Rabbi Yochanan have said that an unintentional act is prohibited, contrary to the anonymous Mishnah in Nazir, even if there is another anonymous Mishnah? As we find in Beitzah (23b): "Why is this anonymous Mishnah stronger than that one?" And Rabbi Yochanan would likewise not rule in accordance with either one without proof. Alternatively, one can say: That which [Abaye stated that Rabba] acted in accordance with the stringencies of Rav was [only] in general [areas of halakha], aside from eiruv and mourning, where the halakha follows the lenient opinion among them. Or perhaps, since this leniency sometimes becomes a stringency — such as where [an area] was prohibited during part of Shabbat, where for that same reason it becomes prohibited for the entire Shabbat — he did not count it [as an exception to acting] in accordance with the stringencies of Rav; for Rav does not accept [the principle]: "Since it was permitted, it remains permitted," nor does he accept [the principle]: "Since it was prohibited, it remains prohibited."
